The garrison keeps a reaction force assigned to the station. {NPC:opfor-commander} will read a comms failure for what it is and push armor and 'Mechs toward the site the moment it goes quiet. The high ground around the node is broken and open, fast going on the approaches and poor cover at the site itself. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Reach the station, confirm and complete the cut at the chosen hour, and be off the high ground before the reaction force closes in. Cut it early and you waste the window. Cut it halfway and the province never goes deaf at all.

objectives.primary: Reach the communications relay and cut off its traffic completely at the designated hour: dishes, trunk conduits, and buried hall feed. Put the {DISTRICT} sector deaf for the required window, then break clear of the site.
objectives.secondary: Confirm the cut is complete before withdrawing. A relay that reroutes through an intact trunk inside the hour is a blackout that never happened, so the team must verify the silence, not assume it.
objectives.bonus: Take the station's current signal codebook or routing schedule intact before wrecking the hall — the intelligence that turns the next blackout from a raid into a switch the SLDF can throw from outside.

complications.name: The Buried Trunk
complications.text: The dishes are the visible target and the soft one, but the traffic does not run through the dishes. It runs through the buried trunk conduits feeding the hall, which are armored and hard to reach, and a station that loses its dishes but keeps its trunk simply reroutes and keeps communicating. The easy half of the cut is the half that does nothing.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The relay is shut down only when both the dish field and the buried trunk feed are destroyed. Destroying the visible dishes alone delays the traffic by a single interval, after which it reroutes. The buried trunk requires reaching the conduit access under the cap and is the harder, decisive cut.

complications.name: The Hour, Not the Day
complications.text: The cut is wanted at one specific hour to cover a separate effort, and silence delivered early is silence wasted — the garrison rigs a workaround in the time before it matters, and the window is gone by the time it is needed. The team must reach the site, then wait and make the cut on a clock it does not control.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Cutting the relay before the designated hour starts the garrison's workaround clock early. The blackout window may close before the main effort lands, weakening the SUCCESS outcome. The cut landing within the designated window is what makes the silence count.

complications.name: Silence Is the Alarm
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} does not need to see the raiders to know the station is under attack. The instant the relay goes quiet, its silence is itself the alarm — a comms node that stops answering its scheduled check is a comms node being destroyed, and the reaction force moves on the silence alone.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The reaction force launches when the relay goes dark, not on visual contact — the blackout the raid creates is also the trigger for the response to it. The withdrawal clock starts at the moment of the cut, not at the moment of detection.

complications.name: Open High Ground
complications.text: The node sits on commanding ground for a reason: long sightlines for its dishes also mean long sightlines onto its approaches. The going up is fast and the cover at the site is thin, so a team that lingers to be sure of the cut is a team exposed on bare ground when the reaction force crests the approaches.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The site and its approaches offer little cover. Units at the station are exposed to the reaction force's direct fire on arrival. The time spent confirming a total cut is time spent in the open, trading certainty of the blackout against exposure to the response.

decisionPoints.name: How to Kill the Relay
decisionPoints.context: The station can be silenced more than one way, and each trades speed against certainty. You have three options. Blow the dishes and the conduit access fast and trust the charges. Take the buried hall and wreck the trunk from inside to be certain. Or split the team, hitting the dishes loudly while a party works the trunk quietly, racing the reaction force the noise will summon.

options.title: Charge the Dishes and Conduit
advantages: The fastest cut — drops the visible dishes and the conduit access in one stroke and gets the team moving before the reaction force can form
Minimizes time exposed on the open high ground at the site
disadvantages: Charges on the conduit access may not reach deep enough to destroy the armored trunk — a cut that looks total from the surface but reroutes underground
No way to confirm the buried trunk is truly dead before withdrawing
options.consequence: You cut fast and get clear quickly, but you bet the blackout on charges reaching a buried trunk you never saw fail. If they did, the province goes deaf; if they did not, the silence collapses inside the hour and the team is already gone.

costs.resource: The cut is made fast and unverified — the blackout staked on charges reaching the buried trunk
costs.risk: Charges that fall short of the armored trunk leave the relay rerouting underground; the team withdraws believing in a blackout that never happened

options.title: Take the Hall, Wreck the Trunk Inside
advantages: Reaching the buried signal hall lets the team wreck the trunk at its core and confirm the cut is total, not assumed
A cut made from inside the hall is the only one certain to shut down the relay rather than merely delay it
disadvantages: Fighting into and through the hardened hall is slow, and the time spent inside is time the reaction force uses to close on the site
A team deep in the buried hall is the farthest it can be from its withdrawal route when the response arrives
options.consequence: You make the cut certain by destroying the trunk at its source, but you spend the time that certainty costs, and the reaction force may be on the high ground before the team can climb back out and run.

costs.resource: The time and exposure of fighting into the buried hall to confirm a total cut
costs.risk: A team deep in the hall when the reaction force arrives is caught farthest from its withdrawal route, the blackout bought at the price of the raiders' own escape

options.title: Split — Loud Dishes, Quiet Trunk
advantages: A loud strike on the dishes draws attention and the reaction force toward the obvious damage while a quiet party works the decisive trunk
Hedges speed against certainty — the visible cut buys time for the buried cut to be made certain
disadvantages: Splitting the team puts a small party deep at the trunk with the reaction force already summoned by the noise of the other
Two efforts at once on open ground means two chances to be pinned before either is clear
options.consequence: You buy the quiet party time by making noise elsewhere, but the noise also starts the reaction clock, and the split leaves a thin party at the decisive trunk racing a response the rest of the team called down.

costs.resource: The team divided between a loud diversion at the dishes and a quiet cut at the trunk
costs.risk: The noise that covers the quiet party also summons the reaction force; the split party is caught deep at the trunk with the response already moving

entries.event: The raid reaches the relay's perimeter and confirms the dish field and conduit layout against the {INTEL_AGE_DAYS}-day-old plan. The designated cut hour is set.
The team is in position on the dishes and the conduit access. The cut is held for the designated hour rather than made on contact.
The cut is made at the designated hour. The relay goes dark and the silence becomes the alarm — {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reaction force launches toward the site.
The reaction force closes on the high ground's approaches. The team must have confirmed the cut and begun its withdrawal off the open ground.
The reaction force reaches the station. If the team is still on the site, or the trunk is found rerouting, the blackout collapses or the raid is pinned on the high ground.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The relay must be cut completely at the designated hour, and the team off the high ground before the reaction force reaches the site around T+20:00. A cut made early wastes the window. A cut left partial reroutes within the hour. A team still on the open ground when the response arrives is pinned on the bare high ground around a node it failed to destroy.

opforSketch.composition: A communications-node guard plus an assigned reaction force. A reinforced security platoon holds the station, with a light-'Mech section (20-40 tons) and a dug-in fixed gun covering the cap, at Regular quality. The decisive element is the garrison's reaction force — a company-equivalent of medium 'Mechs (40-60 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality, reinforced by a mobile armor section (Vedette and Goblin behavior) for speed, that launches when the relay goes dark. Signal-troop technicians at the hall are non-combatants.
opforSketch.behavior: Node-defense doctrine: the site guard holds the cap and the conduit access in place, fighting from prepared positions to buy time. The reaction force reads the comms silence as the attack and drives hard for the station to pin the raiders on the open high ground and re-establish the link. It pushes above all to reach the site fast, accepting a road-march risk to close inside the blackout window. The site guard fights to destruction; the reaction force breaks off only if the station is already wrecked and the raiders gone.

forks.name: OPERATION QUIET SECTOR
forks.trigger: The relay was cut completely at the designated hour, the blackout held through the window, and the team broke clear of the high ground.
forks.consequence: The {DISTRICT} sector went deaf on the hour and stayed deaf, and the separate main effort landed against a garrison that could not coordinate or call for help. The order is to exploit the silence the raid bought — a follow-on strike against a now-isolated garrison post in the dark sector before the relay can be rebuilt and the network knits itself back together. The province went deaf; now the blow lands in the quiet.

forks.name: OPERATION CROSSED WIRES
forks.trigger: The cut was partial and the traffic rerouted, or the reaction force pinned the team on the high ground before the cut was confirmed. The blackout collapsed and the raid is compromised.
forks.consequence: The relay kept communicating through the window one way or another, and the sector that was meant to go deaf heard everything. The team is now compromised on the high ground with the reaction force engaged, and the next operation is to break contact and exfiltrate the raid through a sector fully alert and hunting it, the blackout gone and the surprise spent. The wires crossed; the raiders run.

storyElementSeed: A demolition tech kneels at an opened conduit access in the dark, counting trunk lines by feel against a diagram drawn from week-old intelligence. He finds one more cable than the diagram shows, and has to decide in the next ten seconds whether the extra line is a decoy or the one that keeps the whole province communicating.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Reach the relay and cut it dead on the hour: dishes, conduits, and buried trunk. Put the sector deaf for the window, then get off the high ground. Cut it completely or do not bother, because a relay that reroutes is a relay that still communicates.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Cut off the communications node's traffic completely at the designated hour and hold the sector deaf through the window, then withdraw. Confirm the trunk is dead before you leave — an unverified cut is a blackout the books cannot count on.

REACTION_DISTANCE_KM.unit: km from reaction force to station

inspiration: A route and going reconnaissance pushed deep ahead of a planned offensive: a small element must physically prove whether a heavy axis exists through difficult country — testing the bridges, the fords, the soft ground that a map cannot vouch for — and bring the answer back, where a wrong report sends a whole offensive down a road it cannot use.
skeleton: a small reconnaissance element must push deep into denied country ahead of a planned offensive and physically prove whether a heavy axis exists — testing the load-bearing of bridges, the depth of fords, the firmness of ground a map cannot vouch for — and return with a verified going report, where the answer cannot be trusted unless the element actually touches each crossing and the touching is what risks detection, so the crux is confirming a usable heavy route by ground-truthing it without alerting the enemy to where the offensive intends to come
title: OPERATION HARD ROAD
situation: The planned offensive into {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} needs a route it can actually use, and a map alone cannot promise one. The chosen line of advance runs through difficult country the enemy holds only lightly: broken ground cut by many streams and rivers. It looks passable on the survey maps, but it may be useless once heavy assault 'Mechs and vehicles try to move along it. The planners cannot answer the one question that decides the offensive. Can the bridges hold the weight of assault 'Mechs? Are the fords shallow enough to wade? Will the low wet ground carry a 'Mech, or swallow it? {NPC:intel-source} has plotted the route and marked every crossing, but a crossing marked on paper is not a crossing proven on the ground. The intelligence is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old. Water levels rise and fall, and a bridge rated safe on a pre-war survey may since have cracked, been mined, or been quietly weakened. So this is a going reconnaissance, an old and unglamorous job. A small force moves ahead of the army along the route and tests it, one crossing at a time, putting real weight on each bridge, ford, and stretch of soft ground, then brings the answer back. The catch is that testing a crossing means being on it, and being on it risks being seen. A force that checks every ford and bridge leaves tracks and spends time exposed at exactly the points the enemy would watch most closely if he suspected an offensive was coming this way. {NPC:opfor-commander} holds the country with a thin observation screen and one mobile patrol force. It cannot stop an offensive, but it can catch a reconnaissance. Worse, it can work out from where the scouts probe that the offensive will come down this route. That is more dangerous than a bad route, because it gives the enemy time to mine and fortify the very crossings the army means to use. The terrain is the heart of the problem: soft wet ground in the low places between firmer high ground. So the crossings are both the only reliable footing and the only ground the enemy needs to watch. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Prove the heavy route crossing by crossing, bring back a going report the army can act on, and do it without showing the enemy where to look. Report a usable road that turns out not to exist and the offensive bogs down. Get caught proving the route and the enemy fortifies it before the army arrives.

objectives.primary: Advance along the planned route deep into {DISTRICT} and physically confirm it can carry assault 'Mechs and vehicles. Test each bridge's load capacity, each ford's depth, and each stretch of soft ground, then return with a going report the offensive can act on.
objectives.secondary: Keep the reconnaissance quiet enough that the enemy cannot work out the offensive's intended route from where your scouts probe. A route that is proven usable but whose location is exposed is a route the enemy will fortify before the army uses it.
objectives.bonus: Find a usable alternate path or detour around any crossing that fails the test. A route with a proven way around its weak point stays usable for the offensive even if one bridge cannot bear the weight.

complications.name: The Map Is Not the Ground
complications.text: Every crossing marked on the map is only a guess until the ground proves it. A bridge rated to hold heavy weight on an old survey may now be cracked or weakened; a ford marked shallow may run deep after rain; ground that looks firm may be soft mud that takes a 'Mech in up to the hip. The only way to know for certain is to put real weight on it, and your force is that weight.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each crossing's true condition is unknown until the force physically tests it. Regardless of its survey rating, a crossing may turn out to be usable, barely passable, or completely impassable to assault 'Mechs and vehicles. The going report is only as reliable as the number of crossings actually tested rather than assumed.

complications.name: Touching Leaves a Trail
complications.text: Proving a crossing means being on it: wading the ford, walking the bridge, churning the soft ground. Every test leaves a mark and puts the force in plain view at exactly the points worth watching. The thoroughness that makes the report trustworthy is the same thoroughness that risks the force being seen and the route being guessed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each crossing physically tested raises the chance of being detected at that point and the chance the enemy works out the offensive's route. A report based on more physical testing is more reliable but also more revealing; one based on fewer tests is safer but less certain.

complications.name: The Screen Reads the Probes
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander}'s screen is too thin to stop an offensive but sharp enough to notice a reconnaissance. A clever screen does not just try to catch the scouts; it reads the pattern of where they probe to work out which way an offensive is leaning. A reconnaissance that tests every crossing along one route draws a line on the enemy's map straight to the army's intent.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The enemy screen builds up a picture from the force's probing pattern. A concentrated, complete sweep of one route raises the chance the enemy fortifies that route ahead of the offensive. Probing widely, or feinting at crossings off the real route, weakens that picture but costs time and completeness.

complications.name: Soft Bottoms, Firm Shoulders
complications.text: The country is low, wet ground between firmer high ground, and the crossings are the only reliable footing. That means they are the only ground your force can move fast over and the only ground the enemy needs to watch. Off the crossings the going is slow and prone to bogging; on them it is quick but exposed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Movement off the crossings is slow over soft ground with a risk of bogging down for heavier reconnaissance units; the crossings are fast but watched. The force trades speed on the firm crossings against the exposure those crossings concentrate, with little safe ground in between.

decisionPoints.name: How to Prove the Road
decisionPoints.context: The army needs the route proven, but how thoroughly you prove it is a trade-off between completeness, time, and exposure. You can test every crossing on the real route for a complete, trustworthy report; test only the doubtful crossings and assume the rest in order to move fast and stay hidden; or probe widely across several possible routes so the real one is hidden among the others, proving the road while concealing which road it is.

options.title: Ground-Truth Every Crossing
advantages: Returns a complete going report the offensive can act on with no unproven crossing left in the path
Finds every weak point in time to plan around it, rather than discovering it the hard way under the army's weight
disadvantages: Testing every crossing along one route leaves the clearest possible trail and most strongly reveals the offensive's direction
A complete sweep is the slowest and most exposed approach, with the most chances of being caught
options.consequence: You bring back a report the army can fully trust, but in doing so you show the enemy exactly where the offensive will come. The road is proven, but its secrecy is the price, and the offensive may find the crossings freshly mined and fortified.

costs.resource: the time and exposure required to physically test every crossing along the real route
costs.risk: A complete sweep of one route reveals the offensive's direction to the enemy; the road is proven, but the crossings are mined and fortified before the army arrives

options.title: Test the Doubtful, Assume the Rest
advantages: Moves fast and leaves the lightest trail by testing only the crossings most likely to fail
Reduces exposure and gives the enemy less to read by skipping the crossings the survey rates as solid
disadvantages: A report with assumed crossings risks the offensive discovering, too late, that an untested one is impassable under its own weight
The survey ratings the force chooses to trust may be exactly the ones that have quietly weakened since
options.consequence: You move fast and quietly and bring back a road that is mostly proven, but the crossings you assumed are a gamble. If they hold, the offensive rolls through; if one fails, the army finds out the hard way, mid-route, under full weight.

costs.resource: the certainty given up on the crossings left assumed rather than proven
costs.risk: An assumed crossing that fails under the offensive's weight bogs the army down mid-route on a road the report swore was good

options.title: Probe Wide, Hide the Axis
advantages: Scouts several routes at once so the real one is hidden among the others and the enemy cannot read the offensive's direction
Keeps the army's intent hidden while still proving the route that matters
disadvantages: Spreading the reconnaissance across several routes means less thorough physical testing of the one that actually counts
A wider sweep means more total time in enemy-held country and more total chances for the screen to make contact somewhere
options.consequence: You hide the real route within a wide pattern and keep the offensive's secret, but you prove the decisive road less thoroughly because of the effort spent elsewhere. The enemy is blind to your intent, but you are a little less certain of your own road.

costs.resource: reconnaissance effort spread across decoy routes, thinning out the proof of the real one
costs.risk: A wide sweep that hides the route also leaves it under-proven; the offensive's secret is kept, but its road is less certain than a focused reconnaissance would have made it

entries.event: The force crosses into enemy-held country and reaches the first crossing on the planned route; the going report begins, one crossing at a time.
The force works through the middle crossings; the enemy screen detects movement along the route but has not yet pinned it down or read its meaning.
{NPC:opfor-commander}'s patrol force begins sweeping toward the area of the probes, and the pattern starts to suggest a route to the watching screen.
The deepest and most important crossing is tested; this is the moment of greatest exposure and the clearest signal of the offensive's direction.
The force must be clear of enemy-held country with its report by now; past this point the screen has had time to fix the route or the patrol to make contact.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The going report must be complete enough to move the offensive, and the force clear of enemy-held country, before the screen reads the route or the patrol makes contact, around T+32:00. A reconnaissance caught or read too late hands the enemy the offensive's direction in time to mine and fortify the crossings. A proven road then becomes a prepared trap.

opforSketch.composition: A thin covering screen spread over difficult country: scattered recon and light 'Mechs (20-40 tons) of Regular quality holding observation posts on the crossings, plus a mobile patrol force of light and medium 'Mechs (25-50 tons) and a fast armor section (Saladin tank destroyers and hovercraft) that can move quickly toward any contact. There is no heavy weight forward; the screen is built to watch, report, and harass a reconnaissance, not to stop an offensive. Quality is uneven, better on the patrol force than on the static observation posts.
opforSketch.behavior: Economy-of-force screening: hold the crossings under observation, report rather than fight where possible, and send the mobile patrol to investigate and pin down any reconnaissance it detects. The clever move is deduction. The screen works out the offensive's route from where the scouts probe and reports that upward, valuing knowledge of the army's direction more than destroying the reconnaissance. The patrol presses contact only enough to identify and pin the scouts; it breaks off rather than be drawn into a fight that would confirm the area's importance.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN AXIS
forks.trigger: The route was proven able to carry assault 'Mechs and vehicles, and the force returned with the going report without the enemy working out the offensive's direction.
forks.consequence: The army has a road it can trust, and the enemy does not know it is coming down it. The order is to lead the offensive's vanguard down the proven route the reconnaissance opened, using the verified road before the enemy can react to the weight now moving along it. The road is proven and still secret; now the army uses it.

forks.name: OPERATION WRONG TURN
forks.trigger: The force was caught and the route read, or the route proved impassable; the offensive's road is now exposed, fortified, or simply does not exist.
forks.consequence: Either the enemy now knows where the offensive intends to come and is fortifying the crossings, or the answer is that no heavy route exists here. The next operation is to find and prove a different route under worse conditions: a second going reconnaissance, deeper or wider, against an enemy now alert to the search. The first road failed; another must be found the hard way. The map lied, and the army waits.

storyElementSeed: A scout 'Mech stands hip-deep in a ford in the gray morning while its pilot reads the water level against depth marks painted up the legs and quietly calls the number back over a low-power radio. The whole offensive's road depends on whether the depth he reads matches the depth the survey promised.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Advance deep along the route and prove every crossing carries the weight: bridges, fords, soft ground, all of it physically tested. Bring the report home without showing the enemy where the army means to come. A road on a map is only a guess; bring back a road the offensive can actually use.

is-marik.objectives.primary: Reconnoiter the planned route into {DISTRICT} and verify it can bear assault 'Mechs and vehicles, returning a going report command can act on, and keep the offensive's direction hidden while you do. Provincial command will not march a brigade onto an unproven road, nor onto one whose location has been handed to the enemy.

inspiration: A clandestine exfiltration of a willing defector out of an occupied city: bring out an enemy officer who is offering himself and the keys he carries, where he will move only on his own terms, his resistance handler may already be blown, and a counter-intelligence service is sweeping for exactly this kind of contact — so the danger is the handover and the tail, not the fight.
skeleton: an extraction element must bring a willing high-value defector and the access keys he carries out of an occupied city, where the defector will commit only on his own signal and terms, the resistance handler arranging the meet may already be compromised, and an active counter-intelligence sweep is hunting for precisely this contact, so the crux is judging whether the meeting is a genuine defection or a trap and getting the defector clear through a city net rather than winning any battle
title: OPERATION OPEN LETTER
situation: An enemy officer in {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} wants to defect, and he is worth the risk. He has reached the resistance with an offer. He will hand over himself, his knowledge of how the occupation is positioned, and the access codes to a fortified site he helps run. In exchange he wants a quiet ride off-world before his own service catches him. The access codes alone are worth a battalion. The man who can explain them is worth more. But you cannot take a defection at face value. A perfect trap and a real offer look identical right up until the meeting. {NPC:intel-source} set up the contact through a resistance handler in the city, and that is the first problem. The handler may be compromised, watched, or turned. If so, the meeting is a trap and the defector is the bait. Or the defector is real and the handler is the leak. Your read on the handler is {INTEL_AGE_HOURS} hours old, and in a city crawling with counter-intelligence work, that is a long time. The second problem is the defector's own terms. He will not be grabbed and will not move early. He commits only on his own signal, at a place and time he picks. A man betraying the occupation trusts a clumsy rescue no more than his own service. The third problem is the search. The occupation's counter-intelligence service sweeps the city for exactly this kind of street contact. They do not know about this defector. They hunt defectors as routine work, and a meeting on the street is what they are trained to catch. {NPC:opfor-commander} runs district security and keeps a reaction force on call. The instant a contact is spotted and confirmed, they seal off the block. The city is dense and full of narrow streets. A 'Mech is visible from a distance, and a cordon goes up fast. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, kept light and quiet. Hold the heavier combat units back to break a cordon only if the quiet approach fails. Assess the handler, judge the meeting, and get the defector and his access codes out clean. Trust a compromised contact and you walk into the trap. Spook the defector and he vanishes back into the occupation with the codes still in his pocket.

objectives.primary: Make the meeting on the defector's terms. Take custody of him and the access codes he carries. Get both out of the city clean before the search or a cordon closes in on the contact.
objectives.secondary: Judge whether the handler is trustworthy and the meeting genuine before you commit your force. A trap dressed up as a defection costs you the team and the resistance network behind it, not just the prize.
objectives.bonus: Bring the handler and his cell out along with the defector if the meeting proves genuine but the cell has been compromised. A resistance network exposed by this contact will be rounded up by the occupation within days unless it is pulled out now.

complications.name: The Handler May Be Blown
complications.text: The whole meeting runs through a resistance handler whose status cannot be confirmed from the outside. He may be trustworthy, watched, or turned, and the team only finds out which by the time it is already committed to the meeting. A compromised handler turns the defection into an ambush with the team as the catch.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The handler's reliability is unknown until the contact develops. Warning signs read correctly before the meeting lower the chance of a trap; signs missed or ignored raise it. Committing to the meeting with a compromised handler leads to the FAILURE fork as a sprung ambush rather than a clean extraction.

complications.name: The Defector's Terms
complications.text: The defector sets the place, the time, and the signal, and he will not move before them or be taken against his will. A team that tries to grab him early or force the pace loses him; a man betraying his own service bolts at the first sign of a rescue he did not arrange. The force operates on his schedule, not its own.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The meeting can only happen at the place and time the defector signals. Acting early or trying to force custody causes the defector to call it off and vanish, failing the primary objective. The force must wait and hold position on a schedule it does not control, lengthening its time exposed in the city.

complications.name: The Sweep in the City
complications.text: The counter-intelligence service sweeps the district for street contacts as routine, and the meeting is exactly what it hunts. The search is not aimed at this defector. That is the one saving grace. But it can stumble onto the contact, and a contact it sees is a contact it confirms and then seals off.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A roving counter-intelligence search moves through the district on its own pattern. The meeting's location and how long it lasts determine the chance the search crosses it. A meeting held too long, or in an area being swept, raises the chance of detection, which triggers the cordon.

complications.name: The Cordon
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps a reaction force on call to throw a cordon around any city block where a contact is confirmed. The city's narrow streets make a cordon fast to set up and a 'Mech inside it easy to see. Once the ring goes up, getting the defector out stops being a quiet job and becomes a fight to break out of a sealed-off block.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Once a contact is detected and confirmed, a reaction force seals off the block with armor and 'Mechs at the chokepoints. The extraction then means breaking through or slipping past the cordon. The reserve combat units exist for exactly this. But using them starts a visible fight, and that ends all deniability, the one thing the operation was meant to avoid.

decisionPoints.name: Reading the Meet
decisionPoints.context: The defector has signaled the place and time, and the team must decide how to handle the meeting given the chance it is a trap. Go in light and clean to keep the contact quiet and deniable; cover the meeting with the combat units held close and ready to break a cordon the moment one appears; or watch the meeting first and commit only once the handler and the surroundings look safe, at the cost of the defector's patience.

options.title: Light and Clean
advantages: Keeps the contact quiet and deniable: the smallest footprint, and the least likely to draw the search or confirm a watcher
Follows the defector's terms exactly, reassuring a nervous man and giving the meeting the best chance of happening
disadvantages: A light force has nothing in reserve if the meeting is a trap or a cordon goes up around it
Trusts the handler and the meeting based on the information available, with no combat power to fight clear if that judgment is wrong
options.consequence: You take the meeting the way the defector wants it and keep it deniable, but if the handler is compromised, the light team is in the trap with nothing behind it. This is the cleanest extraction and also the most exposed.

costs.resource: the force goes in light with no reserve to break out of a trap or a cordon
costs.risk: A light team caught in a sprung trap or a thrown cordon has nothing to fight clear with; the deniable extraction becomes a quiet disaster

options.title: Cover the Meet Close
advantages: The combat units held close can break a cordon quickly and pull the team and the defector out of a trap before it closes
Trades some deniability for the ability to survive the meeting turning out to be a trap
disadvantages: A 'Mech force near the contact is harder to hide and more likely to draw the search or alert a watcher, which may spook the defector
Combat units close enough to react are close enough to turn a quiet contact into a visible incident
options.consequence: You buy yourself a way out of a trap by keeping combat power close, but that same force risks tripping the search or scaring the defector off. The meeting is survivable if it goes wrong, but more likely to go wrong because of the heavy units nearby.

costs.resource: deniability and quiet traded for combat units held close to the contact
costs.risk: The force that can break a cordon is the same force that draws the search or spooks the defector; the safety net trips the very alarm it is meant to guard against

options.title: Watch First, Commit Late
advantages: Watching the meeting and the handler before committing spots the trap before walking into it: the best protection against a compromised contact
Lets the team confirm the defector is genuine and not being watched before risking taking custody
disadvantages: Watching costs time the defector's patience may not allow; a man exposed at the meeting point will not wait while the team makes sure
Time spent observing is also time the search has to cross the contact
options.consequence: You protect against the trap by reading it first, but the caution spends the defector's nerve and the time before the search arrives. Commit too late and the defector bolts or the search arrives; the trap is avoided but the prize is lost with it.

costs.resource: the defector's patience and the time before the search arrives, spent watching before committing
costs.risk: A meeting watched too long loses the defector to his own nerves or the contact to the search; the trap is read correctly but the prize is gone anyway

entries.event: The force is in the city and in contact with the handler's intermediary; the team waits for the defector's signal giving the place and time of the meeting.
The defector signals the meeting. The team assesses the handler and the surroundings and decides how to proceed, with only the {INTEL_AGE_HOURS}-hour-old picture of the handler's status to go on.
The meeting takes place; the team takes custody of the defector and the access codes, or the contact proves a trap and the ambush springs.
If the contact was detected, the counter-intelligence service confirms it and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reaction force begins throwing a cordon around the block.
The defector and the access codes are clear of the city, or the cordon has sealed off the block and the extraction becomes a fight to break out.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Get the defector and his access codes clear of the city before the cordon seals the block, around T+18:00. If you walk into a trap, or a contact is detected and surrounded, the clean extraction becomes a fight to break out of a sealed-off block. A defector caught inside a cordon is one the occupation gets back. So is the resistance network that reached him.

opforSketch.composition: An urban security and counter-intelligence force: a counter-intelligence team of plain-clothes investigators and a light security detachment sweeping the district on foot and in civilian vehicles, Veteran quality, armed but not a battlefield threat. The decisive military element is {NPC:opfor-commander}'s on-call reaction force, a company (slightly under strength) of light and medium 'Mechs (25-55 tons) at Regular quality with a mobile armor section (Goblin infantry carriers and Scorpion light tanks) for cordon work, which seals off a block once a contact is confirmed. The investigators find the contact; the reaction force pins it down.
opforSketch.behavior: Counter-intelligence cordon tactics: the investigators hunt street contacts by routine and pattern, confirming rather than engaging, and hand a confirmed contact to the reaction force. The reaction force quickly throws a cordon around the block, using the city's chokepoints to seal it, then closes inward to capture everyone inside. It fights to contain and capture, not to destroy, because the prize is the defector and the network taken alive, and it presses the cordon hardest in the first few minutes before the ring can be broken.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAN HANDS
forks.trigger: The meeting proved genuine, the defector and the access codes were taken, and both were extracted cleanly before the cordon could close.
forks.consequence: The defector is out with the access codes to a fortified site and the knowledge to use them, and the occupation does not yet know it has been compromised from inside. The order is to act on what he brought before the occupation changes its codes: a follow-on strike against the site whose codes he carried, made while the access he handed over is still valid. The letter is open; now the door is too.

forks.name: OPERATION BURNED PAGE
forks.trigger: The contact was a trap, or was detected and surrounded; the meeting was sprung or the cordon sealed off the block with the team inside it.
forks.consequence: The defection went wrong, either a trap sprung or a genuine meeting caught by the search, and the team is now inside a sealed-off block with the cordon closing. The next operation is to break the team out of the ring and salvage what can be saved of the resistance network the contact exposed, with the defector lost or compromised and the cell behind him now being hunted. The page is burned; the team runs and the network scatters.

storyElementSeed: A handler's intermediary slides a folded transit pass across a cafe table without looking up and says the meeting is on for the time the defector named. The team lead has to decide, from nothing but the man's hands and the set of his shoulders, whether the words are the truth or the bait.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Make the meeting on the defector's terms, take the man and the access codes, and get them out of the city cleanly before the cordon drops. Assess the handler before you trust him; a defection and a trap look the same until the door opens.

is-liao.objectives.primary: Take custody of the defector and his access codes at the meeting he sets, and extract both before the search confirms the contact. Assume the handler is being watched until he proves otherwise; a willing defector is the surest bait there is, and the kindest lie.

inspiration: A deception that manufactures the appearance of a popular rising: partisans stage sabotage and unrest across many sites to make an occupier believe a general revolt is breaking out, so it scatters its mobile reserve into static garrison duty and the reserve is no longer free to meet the real blow — where the trick is selling a rebellion that is mostly theater without the reprisals it invites breaking the network staging it.
skeleton: a partisan element must manufacture the convincing appearance of a spreading popular rising across many occupied sites — staged sabotage, false flags, planted rumor — so the occupier disperses its concentrated mobile reserve into static garrison duty against a revolt that is mostly theater, freeing the real blow elsewhere from that reserve, where overselling the rising triggers collective reprisals that break the helper network and underselling it leaves the reserve concentrated, so the crux is calibrating a fake rebellion big enough to scatter the reserve but small enough that the network survives staging it
title: OPERATION PAPER RISING
situation: The real attack on {WORLD} is coming somewhere else. Your job in {DISTRICT} is to make the occupation look the wrong way. You do it by convincing them their own province is rising in revolt. The occupation holds the sector with one concentrated mobile reserve. It is a fast 'Mech and armor force, kept together so it can move quickly to meet any threat. As long as that reserve stays concentrated, the real attack elsewhere has to fight it. Your orders are to make the enemy break up that reserve. You do it by faking a general uprising: sabotage at many sites at once, false-flag attacks staged in the occupation's own name, and planted rumors that make a dozen small incidents look like the first night of a revolt. An occupier who believes his whole province is rising does what occupiers always do. He scatters the reserve into static garrison duty, a platoon to this town and a lance to that depot, until the force is broken into pieces and can no longer move as a unit. {NPC:intel-source} has the resistance network in place to stage all this: cells, weapon caches, and the contacts to spread a rumor faster than a fact. But he warns that the read on the enemy commander's nerve is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old. How much he will tolerate is the whole gamble. A fake uprising walks a fine line. Make it look too small and the enemy shrugs it off, keeps the reserve concentrated, and the deception fails. Make it look too big and he answers a real revolt the way occupiers always do. That means collective reprisals and hostages. The network that staged the deception is destroyed in the response it provoked. The people who sheltered the cells pay for a rebellion that was never real. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the reserve and will not scatter it over a single incident. He scatters it only when the overall pattern convinces him, and he reprises hard when it does. The country is dense towns with open farmland between them. Unrest spreads fast there, and a reprisal column moves faster. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE} of partisan-scale elements, kept dispersed. Stage the uprising big enough to scatter the reserve but small enough to keep the network alive. Too quiet and the reserve stays concentrated. Too loud and you bring down the reprisal that destroys the very people staging it.

objectives.primary: Fake a convincing pattern of spreading revolt across {DISTRICT}. Make it convince {NPC:opfor-commander} to break up his concentrated mobile reserve into static garrison duty. Keep the reserve scattered and unavailable through the whole period the real attack needs.
objectives.secondary: Keep the staged uprising below the level that triggers collective reprisals. A deception that gets the resistance network destroyed has scattered the reserve at a cost the resistance cannot afford and cannot repeat.
objectives.bonus: Lure a piece of the scattered reserve into a prepared ambush as it moves to garrison a staged site, turning the deception's own scattering into a chance to destroy in detail what the concentrated reserve had denied you.

complications.name: Too Small, Too Big
complications.text: The uprising has to be exactly the right size, and you cannot know the right size until the enemy reacts. Too few incidents and he reads them as banditry and keeps the reserve concentrated. Too many or too dramatic and he reads a real revolt and answers with reprisals. The deception has to stay in a narrow band between being ignored and provoking a massacre. The network can only feel its way toward that band, not measure it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a perceived-uprising level against two limits. Below the lower limit, the reserve stays concentrated and the deception fails. Above the upper limit, collective reprisals begin and the resistance network is degraded. Success requires holding the level between the two limits throughout the period, adjusting the staging as the enemy's reactions reveal where those limits actually sit.

complications.name: The Reprisal Machine
complications.text: When the enemy decides the uprising is real, he does not chase ghosts. He punishes the population that hides them. He takes hostages and runs sweeps. The towns that sheltered the cells are made to pay, and the network that staged the deception is destroyed in the response it provoked. The reprisals do not fall on the partisans. They fall on the people who made the partisans possible.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Crossing the upper limit launches reprisal columns against the staged-uprising sites and the resistance network, degrading the network's cells, caches, and contacts. A degraded network can stage less, narrowing the band the deception must stay within for the rest of the period and pushing toward the FAILURE fork.

complications.name: The Fist Will Not Open Cheap
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps his reserve concentrated as doctrine and will not scatter it for a single incident or an obvious provocation. He breaks it up only when the pattern across many sites convinces him a real uprising is underway. So the deception has to be broad and coordinated, not loud in one place. But broad and coordinated is exactly what risks tipping into the reprisal range.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The reserve only breaks up when the perceived-uprising level is sustained across multiple sites, not spiked at one; a single dramatic incident does not move it. Getting the reserve to scatter requires breadth, which raises the perceived level toward the reprisal limit. The two pressures pull against each other.

complications.name: Rumor Outruns Control
complications.text: A rumor planted to make small incidents look like revolt does not stay the size it started. Fear and hope spread it faster than any cell can steer. A population that starts to believe the uprising is real may begin to act as if it is. That creates genuine unrest the partisans did not stage and cannot stop, pushing the perceived level up on its own.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Once the staged uprising passes a certain point, the perceived level builds momentum from genuine popular reaction the partisans do not control, drifting upward on its own regardless of the staging. The deception can be carried past the upper limit by its own success, which means it may need to be actively damped down rather than only stoked up.

decisionPoints.name: Staging the Rising
decisionPoints.context: The network can stage the uprising several ways, each sitting differently in the narrow band between being ignored and provoking a massacre. Spread many small, deniable incidents across a wide area to build a convincing pattern slowly. Stage a few dramatic false-flag strikes to rattle the enemy quickly. Or build it up gradually, starting low and rising, reading his reaction at each step. Each trades the speed of scattering the reserve against control over the reprisal limit.

options.title: Many Small Incidents, Wide
advantages: Builds the broad, coordinated pattern the enemy needs to see before he scatters the reserve
Keeps each incident small and deniable, staying well below the reprisal limit
disadvantages: A slow-building pattern takes time the operation may not have; the reserve scatters late, if at all
Many incidents across a wide area means many cells exposed, each one a thread counter-intelligence can pull
options.consequence: You build a convincing uprising the safe way and keep it below the reprisal limit, but it builds slowly and exposes the network across a wide area. The reserve may scatter only late in the period, or the wide exposure may be detected and unraveled before it does.

costs.resource: the time a wide, slow pattern takes and the many cells it exposes to do it
costs.risk: A pattern built too slowly scatters the reserve too late for the real attack, or the many exposed cells are traced and rolled up before the deception pays off

options.title: A Few Sharp False Flags
advantages: Rattles the enemy quickly: dramatic strikes staged in his own name push the perceived uprising up fast
Scatters the reserve early in the period with few incidents and fewer cells committed
disadvantages: Dramatic strikes sit close to the reprisal limit and can tip the enemy into responding as if to a real revolt
A few dramatic incidents may read as raids rather than an uprising, rattling him without convincing him to scatter the reserve
options.consequence: You move fast and risk the reprisal range, scattering the reserve early if the strikes convince him, but bringing down the massacre if they convince him too well. This is the quickest way to scatter the reserve and the most dangerous.

costs.resource: the deception staked on a few dramatic strikes that sit close to the reprisal limit
costs.risk: Dramatic false-flag strikes that overshoot read as real revolt and trigger reprisals; the reserve scatters and the network burns in the same stroke

options.title: Pace a Rising Curve
advantages: Starts low and builds, reading the enemy's reaction at each step so the staging can be damped down or stoked up to stay within the band
Keeps active control of the perceived level against both limits rather than committing to a single intensity
disadvantages: A gradual build demands constant coordination across cells the network may not be able to steer in real time
The rumor's own momentum may carry the level past the upper limit faster than the pacing can damp it down
options.consequence: You try to walk the band deliberately, stoking up and damping down as the enemy reveals his limits, and it works if the network can be steered that finely. But if the rumor outruns your control, the level climbs into the reprisal range before the pacing can pull it back.

costs.resource: the constant fine coordination across cells that a gradual build demands
costs.risk: A buildup the network cannot steer in real time is carried past the upper limit by the rumor's own momentum; the deception loses control of itself and tips into reprisal

entries.event: The first staged incidents break out across {DISTRICT}; the perceived uprising begins to register and the network watches {NPC:opfor-commander}'s initial response.
The pattern builds across sites; the enemy weighs whether the incidents are banditry or the start of a revolt, with the reserve still concentrated.
The reserve begins to break up into static garrison duty as the pattern convinces him, or stays concentrated if the staging has not yet crossed his threshold to act.
The perceived uprising approaches the reprisal limit; reprisal columns form if the staging has run too hot, threatening the resistance network.
The period the real attack needs closes; the reserve is scattered and held, or it is reconcentrating, or the network is burning under reprisals.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Break up the mobile reserve and hold it scattered through the whole period the real attack needs, around T+20:00. Do it without the staged uprising crossing into the reprisal that destroys the network. Too quiet, and the reserve stays concentrated against the real attack. Too loud, and you scatter the reserve at the price of the resistance network destroyed behind it.

opforSketch.composition: A concentrated mobile reserve and its reprisal arm. The reserve is a reinforced company of fast medium 'Mechs (40-60 tons) and a mobile armor element (Saladin tank destroyers, Goblin infantry carriers, and hovercraft) at Regular-to-Veteran quality, kept together for rapid reaction. Once broken up, it becomes lance- and platoon-sized static garrison detachments scattered across many sites. The reprisal arm is a punitive column of medium 'Mechs and armor that strikes population centers and the resistance network when a real revolt is judged to be underway. Counter-intelligence elements work to tell genuine revolt from staged deception.
opforSketch.behavior: Occupation reserve doctrine: keep the mobile reserve concentrated for rapid reaction and resist breaking it up for isolated incidents, scattering into static garrison only when a sustained pattern across many sites convinces the commander a genuine uprising is underway. Once convinced a revolt is real, switch to collective reprisal: strike the population and the network rather than chase the cells. The reserve, once broken up, garrisons in place and is slow to reconcentrate; the reprisal column moves fast and hits hard, valuing the destruction of the network over the capture of any individual cell.

forks.name: OPERATION OPEN FINGERS
forks.trigger: The reserve broke up into static garrison and stayed scattered through the period, with the resistance network intact and below the reprisal limit.
forks.consequence: The reserve came apart and stayed apart, and the real attack elsewhere faced a sector whose reserve was scattered into a hundred static posts and could not reconcentrate to meet it. The order is to exploit the scattering before it can reform: a real strike against one of the now-isolated detachments, destroying in detail what the deception pried apart. The uprising was fake; the opening it made is real.

forks.name: OPERATION ASHES
forks.trigger: The staged uprising tipped over into reprisal and the resistance network is burning, or it stayed too quiet and the reserve never scattered; the deception has failed either at the network's expense or entirely.
forks.consequence: Either the uprising ran too hot and the occupation is reprising hard against a population and a network that staged a revolt that was never real, or it ran too cold and the reserve stayed concentrated against the real attack. The next operation is to get the surviving cells out and salvage what is left of the network before the reprisals finish it, the deception's cost paid and its purpose lost. The deception caught fire, and the people who staged it pay.

storyElementSeed: In a back room, a cell leader and the partisans' liaison study a stack of the day's incident reports spread across a table, trying to judge from an enemy column's movements whether the occupier has started to believe the province is rising, or has started to suspect he is being played. The right answer is worth a battalion; the wrong one is worth a town.

is-liao.objectives.primary: Fake an uprising convincing enough to scatter the reserve into garrison duty. Hold it scattered through the period, and keep it short of the reprisal that ends the network. Sell the revolt; do not let the people pay for a deception they did not write.

is-marik.objectives.primary: Stage the appearance of a provincial uprising that scatters the mobile reserve and keeps it scattered through the period, below the level that triggers collective reprisal. Command wants the reserve broken up; deliver the deception, not a province in flames for a feint.

DISPERSAL_WINDOW_DAYS.unit: days the reserve must stay scattered

inspiration: A sabotage raid against a captured war factory that must deny its output without destroying its irreplaceable heart: the production stocks, the calibration, the consumables can be wrecked to stop the line, but the precision tooling and jigs are to be preserved because a friendly side means to recapture the plant and run it — so the crux is which subsystem to hit, against automated plant security that never tires.
skeleton: a sabotage element must shut down a captured war factory's output by wrecking its production stocks, calibration, and consumable lines while deliberately preserving the irreplaceable precision tooling and jigs that a friendly side intends to recapture and run, against automated plant-security units that never tire and fight to destruction, so the crux is choosing which subsystem of a working production complex to destroy to deny output without breaking the heart that makes the plant worth taking back, rather than the easy total demolition
title: OPERATION COLD FORGE
situation: The occupation is building war machines on {WORLD} in a factory it did not build. {EMPLOYER} wants the output stopped without wrecking the factory itself. The captured Star League factory in {DISTRICT} is running again under enemy management. It turns out 'Mechs and parts on machine tools that cannot be replaced anywhere in the occupied sector: precision jigs, calibration rigs, and fabrication lines. The old Star League took decades to build them. The SLDF means to take the plant back and run it once the campaign reaches this far. So the order is the hard kind of sabotage. Stop the output now, but preserve the irreplaceable gear. Wreck the material stockpiles, ruin the calibration, and cut the supply lines that feed the floor to stop the line cold. But leave the machine tools intact, because a factory burned to the ground helps no one once it is recaptured. {NPC:intel-source} has the floor plan and the systems mapped: the stockpiles, the calibration bays, and the fabrication lines. But the map is {INTEL_AGE_DAYS} days old, and the enemy moves the floor around as production demands. So confirm on the ground which gear is irreplaceable tooling and which is replaceable stock. Do not blow charges off the diagram. The catch is that the easy sabotage and the right sabotage are two different jobs. Total demolition is simple. You just destroy everything. But that wrecks the very machine tools the operation exists to preserve. Precise, selective destruction is hard. You hit only the systems that stop output and spare the ones that make the factory worth taking back. That means working deeper, longer, and more carefully inside a defended complex. The factory is guarded by automated security. Caretaker units never tire and have no morale to break. They patrol the floor and fight to the death wherever they find an intruder. {NPC:opfor-commander} oversees the site and keeps a mobile response force on call beyond the automated units. The complex is dense industrial ground: tight halls and machine bays where a 'Mech is cramped and slow. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Stop the line, spare the machine tools, and get clear. Destroy everything and you deny the enemy a factory, but you deny your own side one too. Spare too much and the line is running again within a week.

objectives.primary: Shut down the factory's output. Destroy its material stockpiles, calibration rigs, and supply feed lines, but leave the irreplaceable precision machine tools and jigs intact. Then withdraw before the automated security and the mobile response force can pin the team down.
objectives.secondary: Confirm which equipment is irreplaceable tooling and which is replaceable stock on the ground before placing charges. A diagram read wrong puts the demolition on the jigs the operation exists to preserve, denying the factory to the side that means to recapture it.
objectives.bonus: Recover or copy the factory's calibration and tooling records intact before ruining the bays. This data lets the SLDF restart the preserved line in days rather than months when the factory is retaken.

complications.name: Stop the Line, Spare the Heart
complications.text: The output systems and the machine tools sit in the same complex. The difference between stopping the line and destroying the factory is which charges go where. Wreck the stockpiles and calibration and the line stops. Wreck the jigs and the factory is dead for everyone, including the side that means to run it. The whole difficulty is hitting one and sparing the other inside a building where they sit side by side.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Systems are tagged as either output (material stockpiles, calibration, supply lines) or irreplaceable (precision tooling, jigs). Destroying output systems shuts the line down and completes the primary objective; destroying irreplaceable systems denies the factory to friendly recapture and fails the preservation objective. The two are physically mixed together, so demolition must be selective, not area-wide.

complications.name: The Diagram Lies on the Floor
complications.text: The map shows where the tooling and the stockpiles were, but the enemy moves the floor around to suit production, and a calibration bay last week may be a stockpile hall this week. A team that blows charges based on the diagram blows the wrong ones. Knowing which is which means physically checking, on the floor, against the clock, before the charge goes down.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The identity of each system must be confirmed on the ground; acting on the {INTEL_AGE_DAYS}-day-old diagram alone carries a chance of mistaking tooling for stock or the reverse. Time spent verifying lowers the chance of destroying irreplaceable equipment by mistake, at the cost of more time spent inside the complex.

complications.name: The Tireless Caretakers
complications.text: The factory's security is automated: caretaker units that do not sleep, do not tire, and have no nerve to break. They patrol the floor on both fixed and random routes and fight to the death wherever they meet an intruder. They cannot be routed and cannot be waited out; they are simply always there, between the team and the work.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Automated caretaker units patrol the complex and attack on contact, fighting to the death with no morale checks. They cannot be made to break or withdraw; they must be destroyed, evaded, or outrun. Their constant presence sets the pace for how long the team can work on any system before being found.

complications.name: Cramped Ground, Slow Going
complications.text: The complex is dense industrial structure: tight halls, machine bays, and overhead gantries where a 'Mech is boxed in and slow, and the careful work of selective demolition is slowest of all. The mobile response force {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps beyond the automated units exploits that slowness, knowing a team deep in the bays cannot leave quickly.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The complex interior slows movement and restricts maneuver; 'Mechs are cramped and combat vehicles are largely confined to the wider halls. The selective work takes longer than area-wide demolition would, and the slow going lengthens the withdrawal while the mobile response force closes in.

decisionPoints.name: How Surgical to Be
decisionPoints.context: The operation wants the line dead and the machine tools spared. How finely to cut is the choice. Hit only the exact systems that stop output and verify each one. That spares the tooling for certain but means working deep and long. Or hit the stockpile halls and supply feeds hard and fast, stopping the line at the edges and never going near the tooling. Or place heavier charges and accept some risk to the tooling to be sure the output is truly dead.

options.title: Cut Precisely, Verify Each
advantages: Stops the output and spares the irreplaceable tooling for certain by confirming and hitting only the correct systems
Leaves the factory in the best possible state for friendly recapture and restart
disadvantages: The precise work means going deepest and staying longest inside the complex, the most exposed to the caretakers and the response force
Verifying every system against the clock spends time the withdrawal will need
options.consequence: You stop the output and preserve the irreplaceable equipment exactly as ordered, but you pay for the precision in time spent deep inside the factory, and the caretakers and the response force have the longest to find a team working slowly and carefully.

costs.resource: the deep penetration and verification time the precise cut demands inside the defended complex
costs.risk: A team working slowly and carefully deep in the bays is the team the response force has longest to pin down; the precise cut bought at the price of the hardest withdrawal

options.title: Hit the Edges Fast
advantages: Stops the line by wrecking the stockpile halls and supply feeds at the complex's edges, never going near the tooling
Fast and shallow: the least time inside, the quickest withdrawal, and the tooling left untouched simply by distance
disadvantages: Cutting only the feeds and stockpiles may stop the line for weeks rather than for good; the calibration and inner lines survive to be restocked
A shallow strike leaves the deeper output systems intact and the shutdown less complete
options.consequence: You stop the line fast and keep the tooling safe by never approaching it, but the shutdown is shallow. The enemy restocks and recalibrates and the line runs again sooner than a deep cut would allow. This is the safe sabotage and the temporary one.

costs.resource: the completeness of the shutdown traded for speed and distance from the tooling
costs.risk: An edges-only strike the enemy restocks in weeks stops the output briefly, not for good; the line cold today and running again before the campaign arrives

options.title: Heavier Denial, Accept Risk
advantages: Heavier demolition across the output systems makes certain the line is dead, not merely stopped
Trades the fine work for confidence the output is truly stopped for the long term
disadvantages: Heavier charges near the mixed-in tooling risk damaging the irreplaceable equipment the operation was meant to preserve
Demolition placed for certainty over precision is the most likely to take a jig along with the stock beside it
options.consequence: You make the shutdown certain by hitting hard, and you accept that some of the irreplaceable tooling may go with it. The line is dead for good, and the factory may be worth less to recapture, as the price of being sure.

costs.resource: the risk to the irreplaceable tooling accepted to make the shutdown certain
costs.risk: Heavier charges among mixed-together systems take tooling along with stock; the line dead for good and the factory's irreplaceable equipment damaged, denying it to friendly recapture too

entries.event: The team breaks into the complex and reaches the production floor; the identity of each system is confirmed against the {INTEL_AGE_DAYS}-day-old diagram as the caretaker patrols detect movement.
Charges go onto the confirmed output systems; the automated security converges on the disturbed bays and the selective work continues under fire.
The output demolition fires; the line goes cold and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s mobile response force launches toward the factory beyond the caretakers.
The mobile response force closes on the complex; the team must be clear of the cramped interior and moving for the perimeter.
The response force reaches the factory; a team still in the bays is pinned down in cramped ground, and any tooling caught in the demolition is confirmed lost.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Destroy the output systems, confirm the tooling is spared, and get the team clear of the complex before the mobile response force arrives around T+18:00. A team caught in the bays is pinned down in ground a 'Mech cannot move in. Charges placed wrong leave the line running or the tooling broken. Either way, the factory is denied to the enemy and to the side that meant to take it back.

opforSketch.composition: An automated factory security network plus a mobile response force. The floor is held by tireless caretaker units: light and medium automated 'Mechs (25-50 tons) and fixed automated gun emplacements, with no morale, patrolling on fixed and random routes. The decisive human element is {NPC:opfor-commander}'s on-call mobile response force, a company (slightly under strength) of medium 'Mechs (40-55 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality with a light armor section (Goblin infantry carriers and Scorpion light tanks) for the approaches, which launches when the line is hit. Factory technicians are non-combatants.
opforSketch.behavior: Automated-factory doctrine: the caretaker units patrol the complex and attack any intruder on contact, fighting to the death with no morale and no withdrawal, limiting the team's working time by their tireless presence rather than by reaction speed. The mobile response force launches once the sabotage is detected and drives for the complex to pin the team down in the cramped interior; it presses to trap the raiders in ground they cannot move fast in, valuing containment over destruction, since a team trapped in the bays is a team caught. The caretakers never break; the response force breaks off only once the factory is cleared and the raiders are gone.

forks.name: OPERATION KEPT FORGE
forks.trigger: The output was stopped, the irreplaceable tooling spared, and the team broke clear of the complex.
forks.consequence: The line is cold and the irreplaceable equipment is whole, denied to the occupation now and waiting for the SLDF that means to take it back. The order is to screen the silenced factory against the enemy's attempt to restart or strip it before the campaign can reach and recapture it, holding the factory in the state the raid left it. The line stopped; the factory kept.

forks.name: OPERATION BROKEN ANVIL
forks.trigger: The demolition went wrong (the tooling destroyed along with the stock, or the line left running), or the response force pinned the team down in the complex.
forks.consequence: The sabotage missed its difficult mark: the irreplaceable equipment broke along with the output, or the output survived and the line will run again, or the team is pinned down in the bays with the response force closing in. The next operation is to fight the team clear of the cramped complex and salvage the mission's purpose: a second attempt at the shutdown, or an extraction from a factory now fully alert. The mission broke; the team breaks contact.

storyElementSeed: A demolition tech crouches between a calibration rig and a stockpile rack, a charge in each hand and the week-old floor plan in her head. A caretaker drone patrols past the end of the aisle on its tireless circuit. She counts the seconds until it returns, weighing them against the time it takes to be sure which of the two machines in front of her the army wants kept.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Kill the factory's output (stockpiles, calibration, feed lines) and leave the machine tools whole, then get clear of the floor. Stop the line, spare the irreplaceable equipment; a factory blown to the ground helps the enemy and us the same amount, which is none.

is-steiner.objectives.primary: Deny the factory's output by wrecking the production systems while preserving the irreplaceable tooling for recapture, then withdraw. The jigs are an asset on the books worth more than the raid itself; stop the line without writing them off.

inspiration: A raid to seize an enemy intelligence service's archive before it can be evacuated to safety: the occupation's secret-police files on the resistance — the names, the cells, the collaborators — are being moved out of reach on a known evacuation protocol, and the raid must reach and take or burn them before the convoy carries them off, where destroying the archive saves the resistance but loses the counter-intelligence the files could also yield.
skeleton: a raid element must reach an occupation secret-police archive and seize or destroy it before a known evacuation protocol moves the files out of reach to a secure rear, racing the loading and departure of the evacuation rather than a destruction timer, where the files name the resistance and must not survive in enemy hands but also hold the counter-intelligence the raiders' own side wants, so the crux is beating the evacuation to the archive and choosing between carrying the files off intact for their intelligence and burning them in place to be sure the enemy never uses them
title: OPERATION LAST FILE
situation: The occupation's secret police on {WORLD} are packing up their files. The survival of the whole resistance depends on those files never reaching their destination. Over the months of occupation, the counter-intelligence service in {DISTRICT} has built an archive: the names, the cell maps, the collaborator lists, the whole record of who the resistance is and who has betrayed it. Now that archive is being evacuated to a secure rear area ahead of the campaign's advance. There it can be studied at leisure and used to roll up every cell on {WORLD} and beyond. {EMPLOYER} means to stop it. The raid has to reach the archive and either seize it or destroy it before the evacuation carries it off. {NPC:intel-source} has the building, the strong-room, and the evacuation schedule: the loading bays, the convoy forming up, the departure window. But he warns the intel is {INTEL_AGE_HOURS} hours old. An evacuation runs early as often as late, so the convoy may leave early and the window may be shorter than the plan says. The clock here is not a demolition timer counting down. It is a convoy being loaded, and the race is to reach the strong-room before the loading and departure finish. A choice waits at the archive, and the raid must make it under fire. The files name the resistance, so they must not survive in enemy hands. The safe answer is to burn them in place and be certain. But the same files hold counter-intelligence the SLDF wants badly: the collaborator network, the service's own sources, the full picture that would let the resistance turn the hunt around. That argues for carrying the archive off intact, which is slower, heavier, and riskier than burning it. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the service's security and the evacuation escort. He will fight to get the archive away or, failing that, to deny it to the raiders. The city ground is dense, with narrow streets around the building. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}. Reach the strong-room before the convoy leaves, and decide there whether the files leave with you or burn where they sit. Arrive after the convoy has gone and the archive is away to the rear. Hesitate at the choice and it leaves while you decide.

objectives.primary: Reach the secret-police archive before the evacuation convoy departs. Either seize the files intact or destroy them in place. Deny the occupation the resistance's names and cell maps either way.
objectives.secondary: Reach the strong-room before the evacuation finishes loading and departs. An archive already convoyed to the secure rear is beyond the raid's reach, and the operation fails not to a clock but to a convoy that left first.
objectives.bonus: Carry off the collaborator and source files intact rather than burning them. This counter-intelligence lets the resistance identify who has turned and who is being watched, and roll up the occupation's network instead of merely surviving its own losses.

complications.name: A Convoy, Not a Timer
complications.text: The clock here is an evacuation in progress: files being boxed, loaded, a convoy forming up to leave for the rear. It does not tick down evenly. It leaves when it is loaded, which may be early or late. Once it leaves, the archive is gone beyond reach. The race is against a process the raiders can see only in {INTEL_AGE_HOURS}-hour-old glimpses, not against a fixed number on a timer.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track the progress of the evacuation loading, not a fixed timer. The convoy departs when loading completes, on a window that may run ahead of or behind the intelligence. Arriving after departure fails the primary outright, since the archive is in the secure rear. Disrupting the loading at the bays or the convoy forming up can buy time at the building.

complications.name: Carry or Burn
complications.text: At the strong-room the raid faces the operation's real choice. The files must not stay with the enemy, and burning them makes that certain: fast, sure, irreversible. But the files are also worth more to the SLDF intact than burned, and carrying them off whole gives the resistance the counter-intelligence to turn the hunt around. Certain denial or valuable capture, with no time to have both.
complications.mechanicalEffect: At the archive, the team chooses to destroy in place (fast, certain denial, no intelligence recovered) or extract intact (slow, heavy, the files at risk during the withdrawal but their counter-intelligence value recovered if it succeeds). The choice cannot be put off for long; the pressure of the ongoing evacuation forces it.

complications.name: The Escort Fights for the Archive
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander}'s security and evacuation escort are not guarding a building. They are getting an archive away, and that is a different fight. They will cover the loading and fight to get the convoy moving. If they cannot, they fight to deny the archive to the raiders rather than let it be taken. An escort that knows it is losing the files may burn them itself.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The escort puts completing the evacuation ahead of holding ground; it fights to get the convoy away and, if blocked, may try to destroy the archive itself rather than give it up.
