options.consequence: You gain the value of a long stay without its exposure by leaving a device behind, and it pays off if the device stays hidden. But the device is more to build and more to find, and its take still has to be brought home from a distance.

costs.resource: the extra time and the more-findable installation a leave-behind device demands up front
costs.risk: A leave-behind device is more complex to hide and is lost without warning when found. Its take must still be retrieved or transmitted, and each of those carries its own exposure

entries.event: The signals team infiltrates to the command cable and installs the tap. The stakeout begins, and the {INTEL_AGE_DAYS}-day-old report on the sweep is all the team has.
The tap is producing and the intelligence builds; the team waits near the hiding place, collecting the sector's traffic.
The counter-intelligence sweep is somewhere on the cable, its progress only partly readable; the gamble of how long to stay sharpens.
The intelligence nears the sector's full picture. The sweep is closing on the tap's stretch of the line, and the decision to come off becomes urgent.
The team is off the wire with the intelligence and clear, or the sweep has found the tap and {NPC:opfor-commander}'s strike force is closing on the hiding place.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The team must come off the wire with its intelligence and be clear of the area before the sweep finds the tap and traces it to the hiding place, around T+32:00. A stakeout held too long is found with the team still on it, and the intelligence and the team are lost together. A tap found sends the strike force onto a hiding place deep in occupied territory. The team's only safety is to be gone before it arrives.

opforSketch.composition: A counter-intelligence line-sweep plus a mobile strike force: the sweep is a small specialist element walking the cable with signal-checking equipment and a light security detail, Veteran quality, methodical and hard to detect. The decisive military element is {NPC:opfor-commander}'s on-call strike force — a reinforced lance to company-minus of light and medium 'Mechs (25-50 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality with a fast armor section (Saladins and hovercraft) — held back to close on the hiding place once the sweep flushes out the tap or the team. The sweep finds; the strike force kills.
opforSketch.behavior: This force follows line-security counter-intelligence doctrine: methodically walk the command cables hunting for taps, checking the line's signal and inspecting access points, and trace any splice found back to its operators. The sweep does not rush — it relies on covering the line thoroughly over time — but on finding a tap it traces it to the hiding place and calls in the strike force. The strike element commits hard and fast the moment the hiding place is located, prioritizing the destruction or capture of the signals team over holding ground. The sweep is patient and unseen; the strike force breaks off only if the team escapes the area entirely.

forks.name: OPERATION FULL SECTOR
forks.trigger: The tap collected its intelligence and the team carried it out clean before the sweep found the splice; the sector's order of battle is in hand.
forks.consequence: The team came off the wire with the sector laid bare. The unit positions, the reinforcement plans, and the chain of command were read straight off the occupier's own cable. The order now is to act on that picture before it goes stale. Strike a weak point the intelligence exposed, while the enemy still believes his landline is secure. The wire gave up its secrets. Now they get put to use.

forks.name: OPERATION CUT WIRE
forks.trigger: The sweep found the tap with the team still on it, or a contact blew the stakeout; the intelligence is lost and the strike force is closing on the hiding place.
forks.consequence: The sweep came down the wire and found the splice before the team came off it, or a contact blew the stakeout. Now the strike force is closing on the hiding place, and the intelligence is lost. The next operation is to break the signals team clear of that strike force, deep in occupied territory. You save the people if not the take. The wire is cut, and the sector's secrets stay the enemy's. The stakeout is broken. The team runs for friendly lines.

storyElementSeed: In a hide of timber and rock, a signals specialist sits with a headset and a reel of recorded traffic. She listens to an enemy staff officer read off a reinforcement schedule worth a battalion. On her splice monitor, the line-check tone flickers. It might be nothing. Or it might be the sweep, three kilometers down the wire and coming.

is-liao.objectives.primary: Get on the command cable, collect the sector off the wire, and carry the take out clean before the sweep finds the splice. Sit on it as long as it pays and not one day longer. The same wire that gives you the sector leads the hunters straight to you.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Tap the command landline and collect the order of battle, then come off the wire with the intelligence before the counter-intelligence sweep finds the tap. Read the sweep right. A snapshot brought home beats the whole sector lost with the team still on the wire.

inspiration: A raid to liberate a prison camp before its inmates are moved beyond reach: captured resistance fighters and SLDF personnel are held at an occupation camp scheduled to transport them off-world for interrogation, and the raid must break in, free the prisoners, and get them clear before the transport date — where a botched assault gets the prisoners executed and the freed are too many and too weak to move fast.
skeleton: a raiding force must liberate a mass of captured resistance and friendly personnel from an occupation holding camp before a fixed off-world transport date moves them beyond any reach, breaking into a guarded compound and getting the freed prisoners clear, where a botched or slow assault triggers the guards to execute the prisoners and the liberated are numerous, weak, and slow to move under a reaction clock, so the crux is the speed and surprise of the break-in to overwhelm the guard before it can kill the prisoners and the hard problem of moving a crowd of freed captives out, not a fight for ground
title: OPERATION OPEN GATE
situation: The occupier is holding hundreds of prisoners at a camp in {DISTRICT} on {WORLD}. Within a matter of days they will be shipped off-world, where no one can ever reach them. The Amaris occupation has filled a holding camp with captured resistance fighters and SLDF personnel from across the sector. Intelligence says they are scheduled for transport off-world for interrogation. That means they will be moved to the rear, beyond any rescue, worth nothing to the enemy but what can be tortured out of them. {EMPLOYER} intends to open the camp before that date. The raid has to break into the compound, overwhelm the guards, free the prisoners, and get them clear before the transport leaves. {NPC:intel-source} has the camp's layout, the fences and towers, the guard strength, and the transport date. But this intel is {INTEL_AGE_HOURS} hours old, and a transport schedule can be moved up. So the window may be shorter than the plan assumes. Two hard facts shape the whole operation. First, a botched break-in gets the prisoners killed. Camp guards usually have standing orders to shoot the prisoners rather than let them be freed. So the break-in must be fast and overwhelming enough to take the guards before they can turn on the camp. Second, the freed prisoners are the hard part. Hundreds of captives, many of them weak, injured, or starved, cannot run. You must organize them and move them as a slow crowd under a reaction clock, not extract them like a single asset. {NPC:opfor-commander} commands the camp's garrison and a reaction force. That force will drive for the compound the moment the assault begins. The ground around the camp is open. It is fast going that speeds the reaction force as much as the raid. Recommended force: {FORCE_SIZE}, with the combat strength to crack the compound fast and the transport to move a crowd. Take the guards before they can kill, open the gate, and get the prisoners out before the reaction force arrives and before the transport date. Hit it too slowly and the guards murder the camp. Free the prisoners and then move too slowly, and the reaction force catches a crowd in the open.

objectives.primary: Break into the holding camp fast enough to overwhelm the guards before they can execute the prisoners. Free the captives and move them clear of the compound before the reaction force arrives and before the off-world transport date.
objectives.secondary: Take the guards before they turn on the camp. A break-in too slow or clumsy gives the guards the seconds they need to carry out their standing orders. Freeing a camp full of corpses is exactly the failure the whole raid is built to prevent.
objectives.bonus: Get the prisoners' senior officers and key resistance leaders out among the crowd. The occupier most wanted to interrogate these people. Their escape costs the enemy the most, and their recovery is worth the most to the cause.

complications.name: A Slow Break-In Kills Them
complications.text: The guards have the usual camp order: if the camp is about to be freed, shoot the prisoners. That makes the break-in a race against the guards' reaction inside the fence. Move fast and overwhelmingly and the guards are taken before they can turn on the camp. Move slowly or clumsily and the guards get the seconds they need to start killing. The assault's speed is measured in lives.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The break-in's speed and surprise decide whether the guards can act on their execution orders. A fast, overwhelming entry suppresses the guards before they turn on the prisoners. A slow or detected approach lets the guards begin killing captives, which reduces the number freed and feeds the FAILURE fork. The guards' reaction inside the fence is the clock that matters most at the moment of entry.

complications.name: Moving the Crowd
complications.text: The prize is not one asset but hundreds of people, and many of them are weak, injured, or starved. They cannot run; they have to be organized into a moving column, and a crowd of freed captives moves at the pace of its slowest and most exhausted members. Freeing them is the first half of the problem; getting a slow mass of people clear of the compound under a reaction clock is the harder half.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The freed prisoners are a large, slow group whose movement rate is set by its weakest members; they must be organized and moved as a column, not extracted individually. Transport vehicles speed the column but cannot carry everyone at once; the crowd's slow pace is the limiting factor on clearing the compound before the reaction force arrives.

complications.name: The Reaction Drives for the Camp
complications.text: {NPC:opfor-commander} keeps a reaction force that will drive for the compound the instant the assault begins, and the open ground around the camp speeds it along. The raid has only a narrow span between cracking the camp and the reaction force arriving — and a slow crowd in the open is exactly what that reaction force is built to catch.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The reaction force launches when the assault begins and drives for the compound on a clock; the open terrain shortens its approach. The raid must free and move the prisoners clear within that span before it arrives. A crowd still in the open when the reaction force reaches the camp is caught — the raid's combat element must then fight to cover the column at a disadvantage.

complications.name: The Transport Date Moves
complications.text: The off-world transport is the outer deadline, and it is not fixed. A schedule can be moved up, and the {INTEL_AGE_HOURS}-hour-old report may already be behind reality. The prisoners may be loading sooner than the plan says, or already gone if the raid arrives late. The date the operation is racing may be closer than anyone knows.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The transport date is the outer deadline and may move earlier than the intelligence shows; arriving after the prisoners have been loaded for transport fails the primary objective outright. The window between the raid's arrival and the transport may be shorter than planned, compressing the time available to break in and move the crowd.

decisionPoints.name: Cracking the Camp
decisionPoints.context: The guards have to be taken before they can kill, and the crowd has to be moved. The choice is how to crack the camp. Option one: hit every tower and the guard barracks at once in a single overwhelming assault, to suppress the whole guard force before it can react. Option two: breach quietly and take the guards from inside before raising the alarm. Option three: split the effort, suppressing the guards while your transport stages forward, ready to move the crowd the moment the fence is open.

options.title: One Overwhelming Stroke
advantages: Hits every tower and the guard barracks simultaneously — suppresses the whole guard force before it can act on its orders
The surest way to take the guards before they turn on the prisoners, through sheer shock and speed
disadvantages: A loud simultaneous assault triggers the reaction force at the earliest possible moment, starting the outer clock fast
Overwhelming firepower at the fence risks rounds going into the compound where the prisoners are held
options.consequence: You take the guards before they can kill by hitting everything at once. But the noise launches the reaction force at once, and the firepower at the fence endangers the very prisoners it frees. It is the surest suppression on the shortest clock.

costs.resource: the reaction force triggered at the earliest possible moment by the loud simultaneous assault
costs.risk: An overwhelming assault launches the reaction force fast and risks fire into the compound. The guards are suppressed, but the clock to the crowd's escape is at its shortest

options.title: Breach Quiet, Take Them Inside
advantages: A quiet breach takes the guards from inside before the alarm, suppressing them without warning
Delays the reaction force by keeping the assault silent as long as possible
disadvantages: A quiet breach is slower to develop, and if it is detected mid-entry the guards have time to start killing
Taking the guards one position at a time from inside risks a tower or post surviving to turn on the camp
options.consequence: You delay the reaction force by going quiet, but a silent breach is slower and unforgiving of detection. If it works, the guards are taken cleanly and the clock is delayed. If it is caught mid-entry, the guards get the seconds they need to murder the camp.

costs.resource: the speed of the entry traded for the silence that delays the reaction force
costs.risk: A quiet breach detected mid-entry gives the guards time to start killing. It is the slowest, most unforgiving moment, and the prisoners pay for it

options.title: Suppress and Stage the Lift
advantages: Suppresses the guards while the transport stages forward, ready to move the crowd the instant the fence is open
Attacks the harder half of the problem, moving the crowd, from the first moment rather than after the fight
disadvantages: Splitting effort between suppressing the guards and staging the transport puts less weight on the break-in itself
Transport staged forward early is exposed near the camp when the reaction force arrives
options.consequence: You get the crowd moving soonest by staging the transport as the guards are suppressed. But the divided effort is lighter on the break-in, and the transport is exposed forward. It is the fastest extraction of the crowd at the cost of the surest suppression of the guards.

costs.resource: weight taken off the break-in to stage the transport forward early
costs.risk: A lighter break-in may not suppress the guards fast enough, and the transport staged forward is exposed when the reaction force arrives. The crowd moves soonest, at the cost of a thinner assault

entries.event: The raid reaches the camp's perimeter; the guard strength, the towers, and the transport date are confirmed against the {INTEL_AGE_HOURS}-hour-old report.
The break-in begins. The guards are suppressed before they can act on their execution orders, or they begin turning on the camp if the assault is slow or detected.
The fence is open and the prisoners are freed. The slow work of organizing and moving the crowd begins as {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reaction force launches for the compound.
The reaction force closes on the camp. The prisoner column must be clear of the compound and moving, with the raid's combat element covering its withdrawal.
The freed prisoners are clear and away, or the reaction force has caught the crowd in the open and the raid is fighting to cover a slow column at a disadvantage.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The guards must be taken before they can execute the prisoners. The camp must be freed and the crowd moved clear of the compound before the reaction force arrives around T+16:00, and before the off-world transport date. A slow break-in lets the guards murder the camp. A slow withdrawal leaves a crowd of weak captives caught in the open. A raid that arrives after the transport loads finds the prisoners already gone beyond reach.

opforSketch.composition: A camp garrison plus a reaction force: the camp is held by a guard force of motorized infantry in the towers and barracks, with a light-'Mech section (20-40 tons) at Regular quality and fixed guns covering the fence, under standing orders to execute the prisoners if the camp is breached. The decisive military element is {NPC:opfor-commander}'s reaction force — a company-minus of medium 'Mechs (40-55 tons) at Regular-to-Veteran quality with a mobile armor section (Goblins and Scorpions) — that drives for the compound when the assault begins. The prisoners are non-combatants and must be protected, not armed.
opforSketch.behavior: This force follows camp-defense doctrine: the guards hold the fence and the towers and, faced with a breach they cannot stop, act on standing orders to execute the prisoners rather than let them be freed. That makes the guards' reaction inside the fence the gravest threat, beaten only by speed and surprise. The reaction force drives hard for the compound when the assault begins, to catch the raid and the freed crowd, prioritizing the recapture or destruction of the prisoners and raiders over holding ground. The garrison fights from the camp's prepared positions; the reaction force presses to reach the compound fast and catch the slow column in the open before it can clear.

forks.name: OPERATION FREE COLUMN
forks.trigger: The guards were taken before they could execute the prisoners, the camp was freed, and the crowd was moved clear before the reaction force and the transport.
forks.consequence: The camp is open and the prisoners are out. Hundreds of resistance fighters and SLDF personnel are pulled back from an off-world interrogation cell. The occupier is robbed of its captives, and the cause is given back its people. The order now is to get the freed column to safety and scatter it before the occupier can throw a wider cordon around the region. That means moving a crowd of freed captives through occupied territory to where they can disperse and recover. The gate is open. Now the column is brought home.

forks.name: OPERATION SHUT GATE
forks.trigger: The break-in was too slow and the guards turned on the camp, or the reaction force caught the crowd in the open, or the transport had already loaded; the liberation failed at terrible cost.
forks.consequence: The raid came apart at the worst possible point. The guards got the seconds to murder the camp, or the reaction force caught a crowd of helpless captives in the open, or the transport was already gone with the prisoners aboard. The next operation is to break the raiding force and any prisoners it did free clear of the closing reaction. You save what little can be saved from a liberation that failed. The gate shut. The raid carries out who it can.

storyElementSeed: The fence comes down and a raider waves the first prisoners through the gap. She braced for a rush. Instead they come slow and stumbling, holding each other up. Hundreds of them are backed up behind the few who can barely walk. She does the math of their pace against the reaction clock in her head, and keeps her face still while she does it.

is-davion.objectives.primary: Crack the camp fast enough that the guards never get to use their orders, free the prisoners, and move the crowd clear before the reaction force and the transport. Speed is lives here. Slow at the fence and the guards murder them. Slow on the road and the reaction force does.

is-marik.objectives.primary: Break into the holding camp before the transport date, overwhelm the guards before they can execute the prisoners, and get the freed captives clear. Command wants the people out alive. Deliver a freed column, not a camp full of the dead a slow assault leaves behind.
